terms.gloss: The narrators' recurring epithet for Ostap Bender: a master schemer who lives by 'combinations'
terms.why_hard: Literal 'combinator' means nothing in English; the epithet recurs for the whole book and must be one fixed phrase with mock-grandeur

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: The young con man, co-protagonist; also called 'Остап', 'Бендер', 'товарищ Бендер'
terms.why_hard: Spelling must be fixed once across en/zh/ja; Chinese and Japanese have several competing transcriptions

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: Former marshal of the nobility, now registry clerk; the narrators alternate 'Ипполит Матвеевич' and 'Воробьянинов'
terms.why_hard: Name+patronymic vs surname alternation is the narrators' tone device; must be preserved, not flattened to one form, and transliterated identically everywhere

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビャニノフ

terms.gloss: Ostap's mock-corporate name for the two treasure hunters and their 'enterprise' (NEP-era concessions were state contracts with private/foreign capital)
terms.why_hard: Loses the joke if rendered as 'partners'; the NEP business register is the point, and it recurs with the mock titles below

proposed.zh: 特许经营者 / 特许经营公司
proposed.ja: 利権事業者たち / 利権事業

terms.term: директор-учредитель концессии; главный руководитель работ и технический директор
terms.gloss: Mock board titles: Vorobyaninov is founding director, Ostap chief of works and technical director
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered as deadpan corporate titles in a consistent set so later references ('технический директор') are recognisable

proposed.en: founding director of the concession; chief of works and technical director
proposed.zh: 特许公司创始董事；工程总负责人兼技术总监
proposed.ja: 利権事業の創立ディレクター；工事総責任者兼技術ディレクター

terms.term: предводитель дворянства / предводитель команчей / товарищ фельдмаршал / барон-изгнанник
terms.gloss: Ostap's chain of ironic epithets for Vorobyaninov; 'предводитель' means both 'marshal (of the nobility)' and 'chief (of the Comanches)'
terms.why_hard: The Comanche joke depends on the word 'предводитель' being the same in both; pick a marshal-of-nobility rendering that can be punned on

proposed.en: marshal of the nobility / chief of the Comanches / Comrade Field Marshal / the exiled baron
proposed.zh: 贵族首领 / 科曼奇人首领 / 陆军元帅同志 / 流亡男爵
proposed.ja: 貴族団長 / コマンチ族の首長 / 陸軍元帥同志 / 亡命男爵

terms.gloss: Pre-revolutionary yard-porter who sweeps, guards the gate and reports to the police; his basement lodge
terms.why_hard: 'Janitor' or 'caretaker' loses the servile, old-regime status Tikhon still lives in; the lodge is the concessionaires' base and recurs

proposed.zh: 看院人季洪 / 看院人的小屋
proposed.ja: 庭番のチーホン / 庭番小屋

terms.gloss: Housing department of the local soviet, which requisitioned furniture in 1919
terms.why_hard: Soviet acronym; must expand to a short readable phrase, never keep 'zhilotdel'

proposed.ja: 住宅課

terms.gloss: Old people's home No. 2 run by the social-security office (Стар- = старость, соцобес = социальное обеспечение); the text itself uses both spellings
terms.why_hard: Two acronyms for one place must map to one rendering; 'social security' in English sounds like a pension office, not a residence

proposed.en: Social Welfare Old Folks' Home No. 2
proposed.ja: 第二社会保障養老院

terms.gloss: Supply/housekeeping manager, a stock Soviet petty-official post; here also acting head of the home
terms.why_hard: Not 'manager' in the corporate sense; it is a low household-supplies post whose holder classically pilfers

proposed.ja: 総務主任（アリヘン）

terms.gloss: Chapter VIII title: a 'sky-blue', i.e. innocent, bashful petty thief who is ashamed of stealing
terms.why_hard: Modern Russian 'голубой' = gay; the 1928 sense is 'innocent, angelic'; a literal 'blue' or 'gay' reading ruins it

proposed.ja: 気弱なこそ泥

terms.gloss: Contraband moustache dye whose 'radical black' turns green; Vorobyaninov becomes 'the Titanic's victim'; chapter VII title 'Следы «Титаника»'
terms.why_hard: Brand name must stay 'Titanic' with a shipwreck echo; the epithet recurs and the title pun on 'traces/tracks' must survive

proposed.zh: “泰坦尼克”染发剂 / “泰坦尼克”的受害者
proposed.ja: 「タイタニック」/ タイタニックの犠牲者

terms.gloss: Odessa street proverbial as the source of all Soviet 'contraband', i.e. locally made fakes
terms.why_hard: The joke is that 'contraband' is home-made; a reader needs the counterfeit connotation carried in the sentence, not a footnote

proposed.zh: 敖德萨的小阿尔纳乌特街
proposed.ja: オデッサのマーラヤ・アルナウツカヤ通り

terms.gloss: Ostap's catchphrase 'the ice has started moving' = things are under way; a proverb in Russian
terms.why_hard: Must be one fixed phrase for the whole book so readers recognise the refrain; literal 'the ice has broken' is fine but must not vary

proposed.ja: 氷が動き出した！

terms.gloss: Ostap's catchphrase 'the session continues', echoing the Paris chamber president's words after Vaillant's 1893 bomb
terms.why_hard: Recurs as a refrain; needs a set formula, and a parliamentary register rather than 'meeting'

proposed.ja: 会議は続行する！

terms.gloss: Ostap's reproach: petty shopkeeper's mentality, versus living on a grand scale
terms.why_hard: 'Лавочник' carries Soviet contempt for the small trader; 'stinginess' alone loses the class sneer

proposed.en: shopkeeper's pettiness / Learn to live large!
proposed.zh: 小店主习气 / 学着大手大脚地活吧！
proposed.ja: 小商人根性 / 大きく生きることを学びなさい！

terms.gloss: Loose belted Tolstoy-style blouse, standard 1920s Soviet office wear (grey, velvet as a luxury)
terms.why_hard: In modern Russian 'толстовка' means a hoodie; a machine-minded translator will write 'sweatshirt'

proposed.ja: トルストイ・ブラウス

terms.gloss: Toile du Nord, cheapest grey cotton cloth issued to institutions; uniform of the old women and Alkhen
terms.why_hard: Not a colour and not a brand; a rendering must convey institutional cheapness on every repetition

proposed.ja: ねずみ色の安綿布（トワル・デュ・ノール）

terms.gloss: Primus kerosene pressure stove, the universal 1920s cooking appliance and fire hazard
terms.why_hard: Recurs throughout the book; 'stove' loses the kerosene and communal-kitchen connotation; keep as 'Primus'

proposed.ja: プリムス（石油コンロ）

terms.gloss: Soviet honorific 'Hero of Labour' (1927), used by Ostap ironically of the hungover yardman
terms.why_hard: Must be the official title form with capitals so the irony reads

proposed.ja: 労働英雄

terms.gloss: Orlov trotter, the prestige Russian breed raced separately from faster American-cross 'métis' trotters
terms.why_hard: The anecdote hinges on the two categories being kept apart; 'half-breed' or 'mongrel' misplaces the register

proposed.zh: 奥尔洛夫快步马 / 杂交马
proposed.ja: オルロフ・トロッター / 混血馬

terms.gloss: Aristide Briand, French premier and foreign minister famous for a heavy moustache
terms.why_hard: Reader must catch that he is the moustache benchmark; standard target-language spellings exist

proposed.ja: アリスティード・ブリアン

terms.gloss: Soviet acronyms in the dream sequence: Dnieper dam construction, the Butter Trust, the criminal investigation department
terms.why_hard: Book-wide policy needed: expand acronyms into short readable phrases, never transliterate them

proposed.en: the Dnieper dam works / the Butter Trust / the criminal police
proposed.zh: 第聂伯水电站工程 / 黄油托拉斯 / 刑侦局
proposed.ja: ドニエプル建設 / バター・トラスト / 刑事捜査部

terms.term: Марш вперед, труба зовет! / Парад — алле!
terms.gloss: Ostap's military and circus exit-cues: 'Forward march, the trumpet calls' and the ringmaster's 'Parade — allez!'
terms.why_hard: Recurring catchphrases; the circus register of 'алле' must not be mistaken for 'hello'

proposed.en: Forward march, the bugle calls! / Parade — allez!
proposed.zh: 前进，号声在召唤！/ 列队——出场！
proposed.ja: 前進、ラッパが呼んでいる！/ パレード、アレー！

terms.gloss: Opening of the 1920s salon romance 'Бубенцы', sung by the old women's choir
terms.why_hard: Verse must be rendered as singable rhymed lines and marked as a known song, not the authors' text

proposed.en: Hear the sleigh-bells ringing from afar
proposed.ja: 遠くから鈴の音が聞こえる

conventions: Address: Ostap says вы to Vorobyaninov and ты to Tikhon; render вы as 您 in zh and です/ます polite forms in ja, ты as 你 and plain forms; 'товарищ' is always 'Comrade' / 同志 / 同志 and never dropped.
Soviet acronyms (жилотдел, соцобес, Маслотрест, угрозыск) are expanded into a short plain-language phrase in all three languages on every occurrence; no transliterated acronyms and no footnotes.
Dialogue dashes become double quotation marks in en, “ ” in zh, 「 」 in ja; Ostap's recurring catchphrases (Лед тронулся, Заседание продолжается, etc.) use one fixed rendering across the book.

meta.summary: object with keys [conventions, chapter_titles, writers]

terms.gloss: Father Fyodor Vostrikov, the village priest who is the third treasure-hunter
terms.why_hard: Name spelling must be fixed once (Fyodor not Fedor/Feodor); the clerical title 'отец' must stay a title, not become 'father' as kinship

proposed.ja: フョードル神父

terms.gloss: an Orthodox priest's wife (the honorific used for her, not 'mother')
terms.why_hard: A literal 'mother' or 'Mummy' makes the reader think Fyodor is fleeing his mother; it is his wife

proposed.ja: 神父の妻

terms.gloss: NEP-era tax agent of the financial inspectorate, feared by private traders
terms.why_hard: Not a 'financial agent' or broker; it is a tax inspector, which is why the stallholder is buying him beer

proposed.ja: 税務査察官

terms.gloss: a NEP private trader running a market stall (палатка)
terms.why_hard: Not a tent-dweller or camper; a small private shopkeeper of the 1920s

proposed.ja: 露店商

terms.gloss: the railway right-of-way; used as a mock-solemn refrain ('Интересная штука — полоса отчуждения') for the whole world of stations and trains
terms.why_hard: The legal-surveying term is the joke; 'station' or 'railway' loses it, and the refrain recurs, so it must be rendered identically each time

proposed.ja: 鉄道用地

terms.gloss: railway porters, mock-heroically likened to Yermak, the Cossack conqueror of Siberia
terms.why_hard: The name means nothing to the target reader; the sense is 'burly bearded porters with the air of conquerors' and may need a half-line gloss inline

proposed.en: porters built like Yermak the conqueror of Siberia, in white aprons
proposed.zh: 身穿白围裙、活像征服西伯利亚的叶尔马克的搬运工
proposed.ja: 白い前掛けをした、シベリア征服者エルマークさながらの赤帽たち

terms.gloss: chapter IV title and recurring refrain; the 'muse of distant wanderings' that lures people across the country
terms.why_hard: It is a parody of Gumilyov's romantic phrase; keep it grand and slightly mocking, and identical in title and in text

proposed.ja: 遠い旅路のミューズ

terms.gloss: marshal of the nobility, the elected head of a district's gentry before 1917
terms.why_hard: Not 'leader' or 'chief of the nobles'; the fixed English term is 'marshal of the nobility', and the yard-keeper repeats it as a rank, not a job

proposed.ja: 貴族団長

terms.gloss: records clerk at the ZAGS, the civil registry office for births, marriages and deaths
terms.why_hard: The bathos of ex-marshal turned registry clerk depends on the office being humble and Soviet; 'ZAGS' alone means nothing to the reader

proposed.en: records clerk at the civil registry office
proposed.ja: 戸籍登録所の書記

terms.gloss: the former marshal of the nobility, Bender's partner; called Ippolit Matveyevich throughout
terms.why_hard: Name-and-patronymic address must be kept and transliterated the same way in every occurrence; do not shorten to a first name

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビヤニノフ

terms.gloss: fictional provincial capital ('Old Town') where the chairs were confiscated; root of Старгубстрах, Старгуброзыск, Стардеткомиссия
terms.why_hard: Transliterate consistently and build the acronym-compounds on the same stem so the reader sees they are local offices

proposed.ja: スタルゴロド

terms.gloss: Soviet abbreviated agencies: provincial insurance, provincial criminal investigation, children's welfare commission, dairy cooperative centre
terms.why_hard: Opaque acronyms; render as short expanded names so the satire on alphabet-soup bureaucracy is visible but the meaning is not lost

proposed.en: Stargorod Provincial Insurance / Stargorod Provincial CID / Stargorod Children's Commission / Butter Centre
proposed.zh: 斯塔尔省保险局 / 斯塔尔省刑侦处 / 斯塔尔儿童委员会 / 乳品总社
proposed.ja: スタル県保険局 / スタル県刑事捜査部 / スタル児童委員会 / 乳製品センター

terms.gloss: the unnamed district town where the novel opens, in the Gogol/Chekhov 'town of N' tradition
terms.why_hard: 'N' is a literary convention, not an initial to be expanded; 'уездный' is a pre-revolutionary district, not a county

proposed.ja: 郡都N市

terms.gloss: 'non-Party', a standard box on every Soviet form (not a member of the Communist Party)
terms.why_hard: Not 'independent' or 'apolitical'; it is bureaucratic form-language recorded about a dead 59-year-old housewife

proposed.ja: 非党員

terms.gloss: Count Salias (E. A. Salias de Tournemire), prolific pre-1917 historical novelist, here remaindered at 5 kopecks
terms.why_hard: The joke is 'trashy old bestseller sold for nothing'; the name needs a two-word inline tag

proposed.ja: サリアス伯爵の小説

terms.gloss: the contraband hair dye that turns Vorobyaninov's moustache green; a running gag
terms.why_hard: Keep the brand in quotes and unchanged; later chapters refer back to it

proposed.ja: 「タイタニック」

terms.gloss: the protagonist, a charming con man; epithets 'великий комбинатор', 'сын турецко-подданного'
terms.why_hard: Spelling must be fixed once (Ostap Bender) and all epithets must map to him consistently

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: chapter V title and Bender's standing epithet: master schemer, operator
terms.why_hard: 'Combinator' is not English; needs a fixed epithet that sounds grand and ironic and is used every time

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: 'a Turkish subject'; Bender's only stated biography (Odessa Jews sometimes took Ottoman citizenship to escape tsarist restrictions)
terms.why_hard: Keep the odd official phrase 'Turkish subject' verbatim; 'Turk' or 'Turkish citizen' flattens the hint and the recurring epithet

proposed.ja: トルコ臣民

terms.gloss: homeless street child of the post-Civil-War years (besprizornik), a fixture of 1920s towns
terms.why_hard: 'Homeless boy' loses the specific phenomenon; 'street urchin' is closer but needs one fixed rendering

proposed.ja: 浮浪児

terms.term: Может быть, тебе дать еще ключ от квартиры, где деньги лежат?
terms.gloss: Bender's retort to the beggar, now a Russian proverb for 'anything else you'd like?'
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered as a quotable line, plainly, since it is echoed later and is famous

proposed.en: Perhaps you'd like the key to the apartment where the money is, too?
proposed.zh: 也许还得把放钱的那套房子的钥匙也给你？
proposed.ja: ついでに、金の置いてある部屋の鍵も欲しいのか？

terms.term: до исторического материализма / при старом режиме
terms.gloss: Bender's joke for 'before the Revolution', using Marxist jargon as a calendar
terms.why_hard: Render 'historical materialism' literally so the joke of using doctrine as a date survives; the yard-keeper's 'old regime' is the plain counterpart

proposed.en: before historical materialism / under the old regime
proposed.zh: 历史唯物主义之前 / 旧制度时期
proposed.ja: 史的唯物論以前 / 旧体制の頃

terms.gloss: proverb: 'to some a mare is a bride', i.e. it depends who's asking
terms.why_hard: A literal rendering must still read as a folksy saying, not nonsense

proposed.en: To some a mare's a bride
proposed.ja: 牝馬でも嫁と思う者もいる

terms.gloss: Bender's recurring verdict on shoddy schemes: 'low grade, unclean work'
terms.why_hard: A catchphrase; fix one crisp rendering and repeat it verbatim wherever it recurs

proposed.ja: 下の下、仕事が汚い

terms.term: «Большевики пишут письмо Чемберлену» / «Запорожцы пишут письмо султану»
terms.gloss: Bender's planned parody of Repin's famous painting, keyed to the 1927 anti-Chamberlain propaganda campaign
terms.why_hard: Reader needs to know Repin's painting and that Chamberlain was the villain of 1927 Soviet posters; Kalinin and Chicherin are real Soviet leaders

proposed.en: 'The Bolsheviks Write a Letter to Chamberlain' / Repin's 'The Zaporozhian Cossacks Write a Letter to the Sultan'
proposed.zh: 《布尔什维克给张伯伦写信》 / 列宾《查波罗什人给苏丹写信》
proposed.ja: 「ボリシェヴィキ、チェンバレンに手紙を書く」 / レーピン「ザポロージャのコサック、スルタンに手紙を書く」

terms.gloss: Association of Artists of Revolutionary Russia, the official realist art body of the 1920s
terms.why_hard: An acronym with no meaning abroad; expand once

proposed.en: the AKhRR (Association of Artists of Revolutionary Russia)
proposed.zh: 革命俄罗斯美术家协会
proposed.ja: 革命ロシア美術家協会

terms.gloss: yard-keeper/concierge of a building (here Tikhon), a pre-revolutionary institution that survived into the 1920s
terms.why_hard: 'Janitor' or 'caretaker' loses the old-regime flavour; and Tikhon is a recurring character

proposed.ja: 庭番

terms.gloss: a three-rouble note, the tip the yard-keeper got from his master on holidays
terms.why_hard: Money slang; render as 'three roubles' plainly, not 'a fiver'

proposed.ja: 三ルーブル札

terms.term: Красноармейская (бывшая Большая Пушкинская) / улица Ленских событий (бывшей Денисовской)
terms.gloss: renamed streets: Red Army Street, Lena Events Street (commemorating the 1912 Lena goldfields massacre), two Soviet Streets
terms.why_hard: The satire is in the renaming; keep 'formerly ...' in parentheses and translate the new names, transliterate the old

proposed.en: Red Army Street (formerly Bolshaya Pushkinskaya) / Lena Events Street (formerly Denisovskaya)
proposed.zh: 红军街（原大普希金街）/ 勒拿事件街（原杰尼索夫街）
proposed.ja: 赤軍通り（旧ボリシャヤ・プーシキン通り）/ レナ事件通り（旧デニーソフ通り）

conventions: Soviet acronyms (загс, Старгубстрах, АХРР, женотдел) are expanded into short plain-language names on first use and thereafter kept as one fixed rendering per language; never left as bare Cyrillic-derived acronyms

Dialogue keeps the Russian em-dash convention in all three languages; Bender addresses strangers with ты and mock-familiar 'отец/дедушка', so English uses 'old man/grandad', Japanese uses plain form without -さん, Chinese uses 老爹/老大爷
Name-and-patronymic address (Ипполит Матвеевич) is preserved in full in all three languages; nicknames (Липа) and epithets (великий комбинатор, сын турецко-подданного) get one fixed rendering each

terms.gloss: The narrators' recurring epithet for Ostap Bender: a master of schemes and 'combinations'
terms.why_hard: Not 'combinator' (a logic term in English); must be one fixed epithet, lowercase, used identically hundreds of times

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: Ostap's other recurring epithet, from his claim that his father was a Turkish subject (Odessa code for a Jew who bought Ottoman papers)

conventions: Names: keep name + patronymic as the narrators use them; en transliteration with -y- for й/е after vowels (Matveyevich), zh 新华社 standard with ·, ja katakana with ・ and no honorifics (さん/氏) unless the Russian has one.

Soviet officialese (совработники, служитель культа, инвалид империалистической войны) is rendered as recognisable bureaucratese, never smoothed to plain words; a one-line translator's note at first occurrence only.
Dialogue: Russian em-dash lines become en double quotes, zh “”, ja 「」; narrator's mock-solemn asides stay in the sentence without added brackets.

conventions: Personal names: en by simplified BGN transliteration with name-and-patronymic kept where the Russian has it; zh by standard Xinhua transcription; ja in katakana with long-vowel marks on stressed syllables; one spelling per character book-wide.

conventions: Personal names are transliterated, never translated: en BGN-style without diacritics (Ippolit Matveyevich, Ostap, Polesov, Treukhov, Gavrilin, Alkhen; Stargorod), zh standard 新华社 syllable tables, ja katakana; patronymics kept as address, no さん/Mr. added.
Dialogue dashes become quotation marks per language (en "…", zh “…”, ja 「…」); narrator's asides stay in the same dry sentence without parentheses or italics.

Soviet acronyms (Старкомхоз, собес, нэп, Совнарком) get one fixed form per language: a short descriptive noun with the transliterated acronym on first appearance only; wiki artefacts such as 'Категория:…' are dropped from the source text.

conventions: Soviet syllabic acronyms (жилотдел, губплан, Старгико, госпромцветмет): expand in plain words on first occurrence per chapter, then use one fixed short form; never footnote a made-up one — its ugliness is the joke.

Dialogue: Russian em-dash lines become double quotation marks in en, “ ” in zh, 「 」 in ja; Ostap and Ippolit Matveyevich use вы with each other, rendered in ja with polite です/ます and no honorific beyond さん on surnames.

Names: keep name-and-patronymic wherever the Russian has it, transliterated by one table (en BGN-style without diacritics; zh standard 新华社 transliteration; ja katakana with long vowels marked), and render 'вдова Грицацуева' / 'мадам Боур' as title plus surname every time.

proposed.zh: 亚历山大林荫道（现名“无产阶级星期六义务劳动”林荫道）
proposed.ja: アレクサンドル大通り、現在は「プロレタリア土曜労働」記念大通り

terms.gloss: Short side-whiskers in the style of Nicholas I's reign, here on a woman's face
terms.why_hard: 'Nicholas' alone is ambiguous (I or II); the period look is 1830s–50s military

proposed.zh: 尼古拉一世时代式的短颊须
proposed.ja: ニコライ一世風の頬ひげ

terms.gloss: Vox humana, an organ (here harmonium) stop imitating the human voice; Ostap showing off
terms.why_hard: A Latin term garbled into Russian; keep it as Latin, not translated to 'human voice'

proposed.ja: ヴォクス・フマーナ

terms.gloss: 'Whatever God has sent': modest formula for pot-luck; the joke is that God sent Alkhen zubrovka and borscht with prime beef
terms.why_hard: The narrator reuses the formula literally in the next sentence; both must use the same words

proposed.zh: 上帝赏的什么就吃什么
proposed.ja: 神さまのお恵みのまま

terms.gloss: Bison-grass vodka; minced herring spread; small Black Sea sprats (the two kilos Pasha ate)
terms.why_hard: Period foods signal Odessa-Jewish and Ukrainian table; must be recognisable dishes, not generic 'vodka/fish'

proposed.zh: 野牛草伏特加 / 鲱鱼碎（福什马克）/ 黑海小鲱鱼
proposed.ja: ズブロッカ／ニシンのフォルシュマーク／黒海の小魚チュリカ

terms.gloss: The flea market / second-hand bazaar; Ostap's accusation that the extinguisher was bought there
terms.why_hard: Recurs in the novel as where stolen goods go; keep one colloquial word

proposed.ja: 蚤の市

terms.gloss: Institutional blankets woven with the word 'Feet' at one end so inmates lay them the right way round
terms.why_hard: Recurring gag; the word must be short, capitalised and identical each time

proposed.en: blankets woven with the word FEET
proposed.ja: 「足」と織り込まれた毛布

terms.gloss: The old women as 'wards' of the almshouse, a term normally used for schoolgirls; deliberately incongruous
terms.why_hard: Translating as 'residents' loses the mock-orphanage tone that sets up the 'sirоты' joke

proposed.ja: 院の「寄宿生」たち

conventions: Soviet acronyms (Старсобес, губпожар, Доризул): transliterate as a proper name and add a short parenthetical expansion at first occurrence in each chapter only; never expand inside dialogue
Dialogue dashes: en uses double quotation marks with one paragraph per speaker; zh uses “”; ja uses 「」; narrator interjections (сказал Остап) stay in the same paragraph as the speech

Ostap's mock-official speech (вы to Alkhen, bureaucratic phrasing) is rendered in ja with です・ます, and the narrator's voice in plain だ・である form; recurring refrains such as 'пожарной опасности не представляет' use one fixed wording book-wide

meta.summary: object with keys [rank, terms, chapter_titles, conventions, page_types]

terms.gloss: Ostap's invented secret monarchist society; the name puns on the biblical 'swords into ploughshares' (меч/орало) and on орать 'to yell'
terms.why_hard: The chapter title and the society's name recur; a literal 'sword and plough' loses the archaic-biblical ring, and 'orala' must not be read as a verb

proposed.en: the Union of the Sword and the Ploughshare
proposed.ja: 剣と鋤の同盟

terms.term: гигант мысли, отец русской демократии, особа, приближенная к императору
terms.gloss: Ostap's mock-solemn triple title for Vorobyaninov, repeated verbatim throughout the book
terms.why_hard: It is a fixed formula and a running joke; each of the three parts must be rendered identically every time it recurs

proposed.en: giant of thought, father of Russian democracy, a person close to the Emperor
proposed.zh: 思想的巨人、俄国民主之父、皇帝身边的红人
proposed.ja: 思想の巨人、ロシア民主主義の父、皇帝側近の人物

terms.gloss: The narrator's standing epithet for Ostap Bender: a grand schemer/operator
terms.why_hard: Recurs across the whole book; 'combinator' is meaningless in English, and each language needs one fixed phrase with a wink of admiration

proposed.ja: 大策士

terms.gloss: Ostap's stock self-description ('son of a Turkish subject'), i.e. of an Odessa father who took Ottoman citizenship
terms.why_hard: Must not become 'a Turk'; the bureaucratic word 'subject' is the joke and the phrase recurs as Ostap's alias

proposed.ja: トルコ臣民の息子

terms.gloss: 'Bear up / stay firm' — Ostap's meaningless conspiratorial exhortation repeated to every guest
terms.why_hard: It must be one short identical phrase every time, since the comedy is in the mechanical repetition

proposed.ja: 気をしっかりお持ちなさい。

terms.term: Заграница нам поможет / Запад нам поможет
terms.gloss: 'Abroad will help us / the West will help us' — Ostap's slogan that became a Russian proverb
terms.why_hard: A proverbial line; render both variants with parallel wording and keep 'help us' as the fixed core

proposed.en: Abroad will help us / The West will help us
proposed.zh: 国外会帮助我们的 / 西方会帮助我们的
proposed.ja: 外国が助けてくれる / 西側が助けてくれる

terms.term: Полная тайна вкладов, то есть организации
terms.gloss: Ostap slips into the Soviet savings-bank advertising slogan 'complete secrecy of deposits' before correcting himself
terms.why_hard: The slip only works if the reader recognises a bank slogan; keep the word 'deposits' and let the self-correction stand

proposed.en: Complete secrecy of deposits — of the organisation, I mean.
proposed.zh: 存款绝对保密——我是说，组织绝对保密。
proposed.ja: 預金の秘密は厳守——いや、組織の秘密は厳守。

terms.gloss: 'Gentlemen of the jury' — Ostap's pre-revolutionary courtroom address, absurd in 1927 when juries no longer existed
terms.why_hard: Recurs as Ostap's oratorical tic; must keep the old-regime flavour ('gentlemen', not 'comrades')

proposed.ja: 陪審員の皆さん

terms.gloss: The homeless orphan street children of the 1920s, a mass social problem and a favourite target of Soviet charity appeals
terms.why_hard: 'Orphans' or 'poor children' misses that this was a specific, named category everyone was asked to donate for

proposed.ja: 浮浪児

terms.term: дети — цветы жизни / цветы улицы / цветы на асфальте
terms.gloss: Ostap riffs on the stock slogan 'children are the flowers of life'
terms.why_hard: The three variants must share the word 'flowers' so the parody of the slogan is visible

proposed.en: children are the flowers of life / flowers of the street / flowers on the asphalt
proposed.zh: 孩子是生活的花朵 / 街头的花朵 / 沥青路上的花朵
proposed.ja: 子供は人生の花 / 街の花 / アスファルトの花

terms.gloss: 'Proletarians of mental labour' — official euphemism for the intelligentsia
terms.why_hard: Should sound like Soviet officialese, not like a natural phrase

proposed.ja: 頭脳労働のプロレタリア

terms.gloss: Seasonal work away from home; here Ostap's sly euphemism for private trade under NEP
terms.why_hard: Too literal a rendering ('outside trades') obscures that the caviar-eaters are Nepmen

proposed.ja: 出稼ぎ稼業

terms.gloss: NEP-era private traders (Kislyarsky, Dyadyev); Ostap addresses them in the vocabulary of the class enemy
terms.why_hard: 'Merchants' is an old-regime word deliberately applied to Nepmen; keep the archaism

proposed.ja: 私的資本 / 商人衆

terms.gloss: The 'equalizing levy' (уравнительный сбор), a NEP turnover tax on private traders
terms.why_hard: Unexplained, 'the equalizer' is meaningless; needs a rendering that reads as a tax

proposed.ja: 均等税

terms.gloss: Pun on the tax-form category 'кустарь-одиночка с мотором' (self-employed artisan with a motor) — Polesov is a lone mechanic
terms.why_hard: The joke depends on a bureaucratic tax label; a short translator's note is probably unavoidable

proposed.en: a lone hussar with a motor
proposed.zh: 单干带发动机的骠骑兵
proposed.ja: モーター付き一人親方の軽騎兵

terms.gloss: Dyadyev's private firm, a parody of Soviet portmanteau names ('Quick-Pack')
terms.why_hard: Transliteration alone hides the joke; transliterate and gloss the compound once

proposed.ja: 「ブィストロウパク」（速包社）

terms.gloss: 'My business is sixteenth' — colloquial for 'none of my concern'
terms.why_hard: A literal number-rendering is gibberish in all three targets

proposed.ja: 俺の知ったことか

terms.gloss: Wedding-feast shout 'Bitter!' demanding that the newlyweds kiss
terms.why_hard: Must be explained once; thereafter keep a fixed form so readers recognise the custom

proposed.en: shouting 'Gorko!' (the wedding cry that makes the couple kiss)
proposed.zh: 喊“苦啊！”（婚宴上要新人接吻的起哄）
proposed.ja: 「ゴーリカ（苦い）！」と叫ぶ（新郎新婦に接吻をせがむ婚礼の掛け声）

terms.gloss: Opening line of Fet's poem, set as a much-sung parlour romance
terms.why_hard: Ostap is quoting; keep it as a quoted song title, not paraphrase

proposed.ja: 「夜明けに彼女を起こすな」

terms.gloss: Ostap's pet-name signature to the widow ('Your little Gopher')
terms.why_hard: Needs a cute animal name, not a zoological one, and the same one wherever the widow later repeats it

proposed.ja: きみのジリス

terms.gloss: The 'goods famine' — chronic NEP shortage of consumer goods
terms.why_hard: A period term; 'shortages' is too flat to carry Ostap's mock-thrifty joke about chintz

proposed.ja: 物資飢饉

terms.gloss: A vein bulging in the shape of izhitsa (Ѵ), the last letter of the pre-1918 alphabet
terms.why_hard: Needs both the shape and the archaic-letter joke; 'V-shaped' alone drops the humour

proposed.en: a vein in the shape of an izhitsa, the old alphabet's last letter Ѵ
proposed.zh: 一根青筋鼓成旧字母伊日察（Ѵ）的形状
proposed.ja: 旧字母イジツァ（Ѵ）の形に血管が浮き出た

terms.gloss: 'The meeting goes on' — Ostap's catchphrase, later a proverb
terms.why_hard: Recurs to the end of the book; fix one rendering now

proposed.ja: 会議は続く！

terms.gloss: Ostap's shifting nicknames for Vorobyaninov (field marshal, daddy, marshal of the nobility)
terms.why_hard: Each should be a stable word; 'предводитель' is an ex-rank, not a 'leader'

proposed.zh: 元帅 / 老爹 / 首席贵族
proposed.ja: 元帥 / 親父さん / 貴族団長

terms.term: улица Плеханова / бывшая Губернаторская / Карла Маркса
terms.gloss: Post-revolutionary street renamings that nobody, cabby or militiaman, can keep straight
terms.why_hard: Keep both old and new names literal so the 'formerly Governor's Street' joke survives

proposed.en: Plekhanov Street / the former Governor's Street / Karl Marx Street
proposed.zh: 普列汉诺夫街 / 原省长街 / 卡尔·马克思街
proposed.ja: プレハーノフ通り / 旧グベルナートル（知事）通り / カール・マルクス通り

terms.gloss: Soviet police officer (militsiya), as distinct from pre-revolutionary police
terms.why_hard: 'Policeman' erases the Soviet institution; keep one term book-wide

proposed.ja: 民警

terms.gloss: Horse-cab driver for hire, still the main urban transport in 1927
terms.why_hard: Not a 'taxi driver'; the horse is essential to the all-night wandering scene

proposed.ja: 辻馬車の御者

terms.gloss: Yard-keeper/janitor of an apartment house, also an informal local policeman
terms.why_hard: Not just 'janitor': the dvornik chasing Polesov is exercising quasi-police authority

proposed.ja: 庭番

terms.gloss: A loose belted shirt-blouse named after Tolstoy, typical 1920s office wear
terms.why_hard: Not a hoodie (modern sense) and not a sweater

proposed.ja: トルストイ・シャツ

terms.gloss: Narrator's ironic names for Ostap and Vorobyaninov, from Ostap's 'concession' for the chairs
terms.why_hard: Recurs throughout; 'concessionaires' must stay a fixed word and echo NEP foreign concessions

proposed.zh: 特许经营人 / 合伙人
proposed.ja: 利権屋たち / 相棒たち

terms.gloss: Suburb of the fictional Stargorod, seen from the train
terms.why_hard: Fictional place; transliterate consistently

proposed.ja: グシシチェ

terms.gloss: The Stargorod hotel and restaurant, pretentiously named
terms.why_hard: Keep the quotation-marked proper names, not 'the Sorbonne' as the university

proposed.en: the Sorbonne hotel / the Phoenix restaurant
proposed.ja: ホテル「ソルボンヌ」／レストラン「フェニックス」

terms.gloss: Two overgrown provincial youths, always named by childish diminutives
terms.why_hard: The diminutives are the characterisation; do not normalise to Nikolai/Vladimir

proposed.ja: ニケーシャとヴラージャ

conventions: Forms of address are a running joke and must stay distinct: гражданин = citizen/公民/市民, товарищ = comrade/同志/同志, господин/господа = Mr./gentlemen/先生/紳士諸君; Ostap's slips between them are kept, not smoothed.
Ostap's fixed formulas (giant of thought..., Bear up, The West will help us, gentlemen of the jury, The meeting goes on) are rendered by one identical phrase every occurrence in each language.

Dialogue dashes become target quotation marks (“ ” en, “” zh, 「」 ja); names are transliterated by one standard table per language (BGN/PCGN en, 新华社 table zh, katakana ja), patronymics kept, and Ostap addresses Vorobyaninov with вы rendered in Japanese as polite -ます form with mock deference.

meta.summary: object with keys [rank, terms, chapter_titles, conventions, page_types]

terms.gloss: The con man hero, 'the great schemer'; surname German-Jewish, first name Ukrainian; Vorobyaninov later calls him 'Bender' or 'Ostap'.
terms.why_hard: Transliteration must be fixed once (Bender not Bendr/Benders); zh/ja must not vary between Остап and Бендер forms across pages.

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: Former district marshal of the nobility, now a Soviet registry clerk, hunting his mother-in-law's jewels.
terms.why_hard: Narrator alternates 'Ипполит Матвеевич' (name+patronymic) and 'Воробьянинов'; both must map to one stable form and the patronymic must not be dropped or turned into a surname.

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビヤニノフ

terms.gloss: Vorobyaninov's late mother-in-law (тёща), who sewed the jewels into a chair.
terms.why_hard: Appears only as name+patronymic or as 'теща'; keep one transliteration and render 'теща' as mother-in-law, never 'aunt'.

proposed.zh: 克拉夫季娅·伊万诺夫娜
proposed.ja: クラヴジヤ・イヴァーノヴナ

terms.gloss: Tikhon's job: the yard-keeper/caretaker of a house, who in tsarist times swept, kept the gate and reported to the police; earned medals for service.
terms.why_hard: 'Janitor' or 'doorman' loses the courtyard/street role and the pre-revolutionary police-auxiliary flavour that makes his medal obsession funny.

proposed.ja: 庭番

terms.gloss: The yard-keeper's basement lodge where Ostap and Vorobyaninov meet; recurring setting in chapters 5-6.
terms.why_hard: Must be derived consistently from the rendering of дворник; not 'porter's lodge' in one place and 'basement' in another.

proposed.ja: 庭番小屋

terms.gloss: Tikhon's word for his former master Vorobyaninov; the pre-revolutionary landowner/gentleman as addressed by servants.
terms.why_hard: 'Sir' or 'boss' erases the serf-era servility; the joke is that Tikhon still says it in 1927.

proposed.ja: 旦那様

terms.gloss: Marshal of the nobility, elected head of the gentry of a district (уезд) or province; Vorobyaninov's old post, here 'бывший предводитель'.
terms.why_hard: Not a military rank; 'leader of the nobility' sounds like a party, 'marshal' alone sounds like an army rank (which Ostap exploits with 'фельдмаршал').

proposed.ja: 貴族団長

terms.gloss: Ostap's mock title for Vorobyaninov: 'district marshal of the Comanches', fusing his gentry title with a Wild-West tribe.
terms.why_hard: The pun only lands if 'уездный предводитель' is the same phrase used for his real title; Vorobyaninov's offence at the nickname must remain intelligible.

proposed.ja: コマンチ族の郡貴族団長

terms.gloss: Ostap's recurring epithet and the chapter-5 title: the grand schemer, the man of combinations.
terms.why_hard: 'Combinator' is not English; 'smooth operator' loses the chess-like 'combination' sense; the epithet recurs all book long and must be identical each time.

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: Ostap's catchphrase: 'the ice has broken, gentlemen of the jury' — things are moving; the jury address is pure mock-solemnity.
terms.why_hard: Became a Russian proverb; must be rendered word-for-word identically every time (also in the shortened 'Ну что, тронулся лед?' / 'Тронулся.').

proposed.en: The ice has broken, gentlemen of the jury!
proposed.zh: 坚冰已破，陪审员先生们！
proposed.ja: 氷が動き出しましたぞ、陪審員諸君！

terms.gloss: Ostap's second recurring catchphrase, 'the session continues', as if chairing a meeting.
terms.why_hard: Ordinary bureaucratic phrase in Russian; needs one fixed rendering so the reader recognises the refrain.

proposed.ja: 審議を続行します。

terms.term: ключ от квартиры, где деньги лежат
terms.gloss: Ostap's sarcasm 'and give you the key to the flat where the money is', i.e. you want everything for nothing; became a proverb.
terms.why_hard: Reappears in the haggling ('И ключ от квартиры?'); the elliptical repeat only works if the first full phrase is memorable and reused verbatim.

proposed.en: the key to the flat where the money is kept
proposed.zh: 还得把放钱的那套房子的钥匙也给你
proposed.ja: 金の置いてある部屋の鍵まで

terms.gloss: State Political Directorate, the Soviet secret police of the 1920s (successor of the Cheka, predecessor of NKVD).
terms.why_hard: Expanding it every time kills the joke's rhythm; leaving 'GPU' bare means nothing to a non-specialist — fix a short form and gloss it once.

proposed.zh: 国家政治保卫局（格别乌）
proposed.ja: ゲーペーウー（国家政治保安部）

terms.gloss: A White émigré who fled after the Revolution; being one, or returning, was politically dangerous in 1927.
terms.why_hard: 'Immigrant' inverts it and 'emigrant' is too neutral; the target reader must feel why Vorobyaninov panics at the word.

proposed.ja: 亡命者

terms.gloss: Ostap's parody of the pre-revolutionary romance 'Белой акации гроздья душистые', a song beloved of the White émigration.
terms.why_hard: A literal 'white acacia, flowers of emigration' reads as nonsense unless the reader is told it is a twisted song line; needs a short note or a recognisably song-like rendering.

proposed.ja: 「白きアカシア、亡命の花よ……」

terms.gloss: NEP-era word for a business concession leased by the state to private or foreign capital; Ostap calls the treasure hunt a концессия and himself its 'непосредственный участник' and 'технический руководитель'.
terms.why_hard: Recurs throughout the book ('концессионеры'); the mock-corporate register must be kept with one word, not paraphrased as 'venture' here and 'partnership' there.

proposed.ja: コンセッション（利権事業）

terms.gloss: Abbreviation for social insurance (социальное страхование), the payroll contribution an employer owed in the 1920s.
terms.why_hard: The joke is Ostap talking like a Soviet employee negotiating benefits; a vague 'insurance' loses the bureaucratic acronym flavour.

proposed.ja: 社会保険料

terms.gloss: Ukrainian SSR abbreviation for дом принудительных работ, a forced-labour prison; Ostap's Slavuta anecdote uses it.
terms.why_hard: Not a standard Russian word; a translator may not recognise it as a prison at all.

proposed.ja: 強制労働所

terms.gloss: A black-market currency dealer and the illegal currency exchange of NEP Moscow.
terms.why_hard: 'Exchange' suggests a legal stock market; both terms belong to the criminal-economy vocabulary that recurs in the book.

proposed.zh: 倒卖外汇的投机商 / 黑市交易所
proposed.ja: 闇の両替屋 / 闇取引所

terms.gloss: Ostap's mock-Marxist periodisation, 'before the age of historical materialism', i.e. before the Revolution.
terms.why_hard: Recurs in Ostap's speech; must stay a stiff ideological phrase, not be smoothed to 'in the old days'.

proposed.en: before the age of historical materialism
proposed.zh: 在历史唯物主义时代之前
proposed.ja: 史的唯物論の時代以前に

terms.gloss: Ostap's pet malapropism, using 'congenial' (kindred in spirit) to mean 'brilliant'.
terms.why_hard: Rendering it as 'brilliant' loses the pretentious misuse; needs one odd-but-readable word used every time.

proposed.ja: コンゲニアルだ！

terms.gloss: Ostap greeting the drunk yard-keeper in newspaper-slogan style: 'proletarian of mental labour, worker of the broom'.
terms.why_hard: Parody of Soviet press honorifics; must sound like a slogan, not a description.

proposed.en: Proletarian of mental labour! Worker of the broom!
proposed.zh: 脑力劳动的无产者！扫帚工作者！
proposed.ja: 知的労働のプロレタリアよ！箒の労働者よ！

terms.gloss: Vorobyaninov says he is a 'subject' of the RSFSR, using the tsarist word instead of the Soviet 'citizen'.
terms.why_hard: Translating as 'citizen' erases the slip that betrays his old-regime habits.

proposed.zh: 俄罗斯苏维埃联邦社会主义共和国的臣民
proposed.ja: ロシア共和国の臣民

terms.gloss: Andy Tucker, the swindler in O. Henry's 'The Gentle Grafter', whom Ostap quotes as an authority.
terms.why_hard: Must be recognised as O. Henry's character, not a random acquaintance; transliterate back to the English name.

proposed.ja: アンディ・タッカー

terms.gloss: The anonymous provincial town where the story opens (Vorobyaninov's home town); a literary convention from Gogol on.
terms.why_hard: Keep the Latin letter N, not 'a certain town'; the same convention covers the joke names Кологрив, Моршанск, Славута, which are real backwaters and should be transliterated, not glossed.

proposed.ja: N市

terms.gloss: Ostap's orange lace-up boots, his signature garment across the book.
terms.why_hard: 'Shoes' vs 'boots' vs 'brogues' must be settled once; the colour word must match Ostap's other orange items later.

proposed.ja: オレンジ色の編み上げ靴

terms.gloss: Vorobyaninov's 'moon-coloured' waistcoat introduced in chapter 1 and recalled here as 'известный читателю'.
terms.why_hard: Back-reference; the same adjective must be used as in chapter 1 or the callback is lost.

proposed.ja: 月光色のチョッキ

terms.gloss: A popular late-19th-century urban song ('There were merry days'), which the drunk Tikhon bellows.
terms.why_hard: The stutter 'Бывывывали' and the fact that it is a known song both need carrying; a literal line with the slur reproduced is enough.

proposed.ja: 「た、た、楽しい日々もあったのさ……」

terms.gloss: Pre-revolutionary land unit, about 1.09 hectares; 'урожай с пятисот десятин' measures a jewel's cost in a harvest.
terms.why_hard: Converting to acres or hectares in-line breaks the period voice; transliterate and gloss once.

proposed.ja: デシャチーナ

conventions: Address: Ostap says вы to Vorobyaninov and ты to Tikhon; Tikhon says ты to Ostap and calls Vorobyaninov барин. English keeps names/titles to signal this; Japanese: Ostap→Vorobyaninov mocking です/ます, Ostap→Tikhon plain form, Tikhon→Vorobyaninov 旦那様 with keigo; Chinese uses 您 only from Ostap to Vorobyaninov.

Dialogue: Russian em-dash lines become double quotation marks in English and Chinese (“ ”) and 「 」 in Japanese; Ostap's fixed catchphrases (Лед тронулся…, Заседание продолжается, конгениально, ключ от квартиры…) are rendered identically wherever they recur.

Soviet acronyms (ГПУ, соцстрах, РСФСР, допр) keep a short transliterated/abbreviated form in the text with a one-line translator's note at first occurrence only; wiki residue such as the line 'Категория:Двенадцать стульев (Ильф и Петров)' is not source text and is dropped.

conventions: Dialogue: Russian dashes become double quotation marks in en, “” in zh, 「」 in ja; the narrator's parenthetical asides stay inside the sentence, never footnoted.

Names: en uses a fixed popular transliteration (Fyodor, Ippolit Matveyevich, Vorobyaninov); zh uses 新华社 standard forms with · between name parts; ja uses katakana with long-vowel marks; clerical 'отец' is Father/神父/神父, never 'Reverend' or 司祭 in address.

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: The Stargorod locksmith-intellectual and self-appointed expert on everything mechanical; here tossed in the air twice and tailing Vorobyaninov.
terms.why_hard: The name-and-patronymic form is the narrator's mock-respectful default and must stay full, not shortened to 'Polesov' at random.

proposed.zh: 维克托·米哈伊洛维奇·波列索夫
proposed.ja: ヴィクトル・ミハイロヴィチ・ポレーソフ

terms.gloss: Engineer Treukhov, the chief engineer who builds the Stargorod tram after years of dreaming of it.
terms.why_hard: Consistent transliteration; also 'инженер Треухов' and 'главный инженер' are his labels and should not become 'Mr Treukhov'.

proposed.ja: トレウーホフ

terms.gloss: Chairman of Starkomkhoz, the blunt ex-worker official who backs the tram and cannot stop talking about the international situation.
terms.why_hard: His speech is ungrammatical Soviet-official Russian (благодаря кого, из депа); the translation must keep him folksy and slightly wrong without making him stupid.

proposed.ja: ガヴリーリン

terms.gloss: Stargorod Communal Economy Department, the municipal utilities and housing office Gavrilin chairs.
terms.why_hard: Raw 'Starkomkhoz' means nothing to the reader, while 'city council' is wrong; a descriptive name plus the transliterated acronym on first use.

proposed.zh: 斯塔尔戈罗德市政公用事业局
proposed.ja: スタルゴロド市公共事業局

terms.gloss: Provincial (guberniya) executive committee of soviets, the top local government body of the 1920s; its президиум decides the tram question.
terms.why_hard: Abbreviation of губернский исполнительный комитет; must be rendered as a body, not left as an acronym, and 'province' must be used consistently for губерния throughout.

proposed.ja: 県執行委員会

terms.gloss: Народный комиссариат путей сообщения, the People's Commissariat of Transport (railways), a possible shareholder in the tram company.
terms.why_hard: A four-letter acronym opaque in any target script; expand on first mention and keep one short form afterwards.

proposed.ja: 交通人民委員部

terms.gloss: The state Food Trust, a 1920s trust of food-industry enterprises; haggles down its share of tram stock.
terms.why_hard: Portmanteau of пищевой трест; 'Food Trust' is fine but should not be confused with a charity 'trust'.

proposed.ja: 食品トラスト

terms.gloss: The central union of dairy cooperatives (butter marketing), another prospective shareholder; its representative later gives an unwanted speech.
terms.why_hard: 'Oil Centre' is the trap: масло here is butter; a dairy-cooperative body, not a petroleum office.

proposed.ja: バター協同組合中央会（マスロツェントル）

terms.gloss: Губернская контрольная комиссия, the Party's provincial control (disciplinary) commission, to which Gavrilin is summoned for arm-twisting.
terms.why_hard: Not a court or auditor: a Party disciplinary body; the joke is that pressuring shareholders gets him a Party reprimand.

proposed.ja: 県党統制委員会

terms.gloss: Workers of the Stargorod rope works; their factory is a prospective shareholder and their band plays at the opening.
terms.why_hard: Not 'ropemakers' as a craft guild but a factory workforce that appears as a corporate actor ('the rope works').

proposed.ja: ロープ工場

terms.gloss: Gavrilin's pet saying, 'this is not like buying a donkey'; ешак is a Turkestan-Russian word for donkey, marking him as an ex-Central Asian worker.
terms.why_hard: Appears twice on these pages (once as the opening of his speech, which Bender laughs at) and must be word-for-word identical both times; the dialectal донkey word should sound homely, not exotic.

proposed.en: This isn't like buying a donkey, you know
proposed.zh: 这可不是买头毛驴那么简单
proposed.ja: ロバを一頭買うのとはわけが違うぞ

terms.gloss: The Stargorod feuilletonist, town-famous under the nickname 'Prince of Denmark' (Hamlet), who now signs himself 'Flywheel'.
terms.why_hard: Both names are jokes and must be translated, not transliterated; the narrator combines them (Принц-Маховик, Маховик-Датский) so the two renderings must be short enough to hyphenate.

proposed.ja: デンマークの王子 / はずみ車

terms.gloss: The local newspaper, a provincial clone of Pravda, whose third page carries the tram sketches.
terms.why_hard: Pravda should stay recognisable as the national paper's name, not be translated as 'Truth'.

proposed.ja: 『スタルゴロド・プラウダ』

terms.gloss: The 'sketch of everyday life', a standard 1920s Soviet newspaper genre of upbeat reportage; the book parodies its headlines and cliches.
terms.why_hard: 'Essay' or 'feature' loses the genre; the target reader needs a phrase that sounds like newsroom jargon.

proposed.ja: 生活ルポ

terms.term: На берегу пустынных волн стоял он, дум великих полн
terms.gloss: Opening lines of Pushkin's 'The Bronze Horseman' (Peter the Great on the Neva shore), quoted by Flywheel about a snub-nosed engineer on the rafters.
terms.why_hard: Must be recognisable as Pushkin and slightly grandiose; use one fixed rendering (Pushkin recurs in the book) and name the source in a bracket, not a footnote.

proposed.en: 'On the shore of desolate waves he stood, full of lofty thoughts' (Pushkin, The Bronze Horseman)
proposed.zh: “他伫立在荒凉的波涛岸边，满怀宏伟的思想”（普希金《青铜骑士》）
proposed.ja: 「荒涼たる波の岸辺に彼は立ち、大いなる思いに満ちて」（プーシキン『青銅の騎士』）

terms.gloss: Peaked cap with the crossed-hammers badge worn by engineers and railway/technical staff in Russia since tsarist times.
terms.why_hard: Not 'a cap with little hammers on it': the badge marks him as an engineer, which is the point of the sketch.

proposed.en: a shabby engineer's cap with the crossed-hammers badge
proposed.zh: 一顶带交叉小锤徽章的旧工程师制帽
proposed.ja: 交差した小槌の徽章のついたよれよれの技師帽

terms.gloss: Truncated pre-revolutionary formal letter closing ('Accept the assurance of..., etc.'), used by Treukhov to end his sarcastic rebuttal.
terms.why_hard: Should sound like an old-fashioned business-letter formula cut short, not like a shrug.

proposed.ja: 敬具、云々。

terms.gloss: 'Comrade', abbreviated 'т.' in newspaper and official prose (т. Маховика, т. Гаврилина, т. Мосина).
terms.why_hard: Full 'Comrade' in dialogue but the clipped 'т.' in mock-journalese is part of the parody; the abbreviation needs one fixed form per language.

proposed.zh: 同志（引用报纸文体时置于姓后）
proposed.ja: 同志（新聞文体の引用では姓の後に「同志」）

terms.term: не за страх, а за совесть
terms.gloss: Set phrase 'not from fear but from conscience', i.e. wholeheartedly; Gavrilin splits it with 'товарищи'.
terms.why_hard: Literal rendering reads oddly; the translation must keep it a recognisable cliche and allow the interrupting 'comrades'.

proposed.en: not for fear but, comrades, for conscience' sake
proposed.zh: 不是出于害怕，同志们，而是出于良心
proposed.ja: 恐れからではなく、同志諸君、良心から

terms.gloss: Stock stenographic formula of Soviet reporting ('stormy applause turning into an ovation'), pencilled in by both journalists over thin clapping.
terms.why_hard: Must sound like the canonical minutes-of-a-meeting cliche so the joke of one journalist crossing 'ovation' out works.

proposed.en: Stormy applause, turning into an ovation
proposed.zh: 热烈的掌声，转为经久不息的欢呼
proposed.ja: 嵐のような拍手、それは歓呼へと変わる

terms.term: Чемберлен, сенатор Бора, румынские бояре, Муссолини
terms.gloss: The stock villains of 1927 Soviet 'international situation' speeches: Austen Chamberlain (British break with the USSR), US Senator Borah, Romania's landowners (Bessarabia), Mussolini.
terms.why_hard: Chamberlain must be Austen, not Neville; 'boyars' is Soviet propaganda shorthand for Romania's ruling class, not medieval nobles.

proposed.en: Chamberlain, Senator Borah, the Romanian boyars, Mussolini
proposed.zh: 张伯伦、参议员博拉、罗马尼亚贵族老爷、墨索里尼
proposed.ja: チェンバレン、ボーラ上院議員、ルーマニアの貴族ども、ムッソリーニ

terms.term: акробаты пера, виртуозы фарса, шакалы ротационных машин
terms.gloss: The French communist's anti-bourgeois-press tirade recalled by Treukhov; 'jackals of the rotary presses' became a Russian proverb for hack journalists.
terms.why_hard: Translate literally and rhythmically; the phrase must be quotable, as it is in Russian.

proposed.en: these acrobats of the pen, these virtuosi of farce, these jackals of the rotary press
proposed.zh: 这些笔杆子的杂技演员，这些闹剧的名手，这些轮转印刷机的豺狼
proposed.ja: このペンの曲芸師ども、笑劇の名手ども、輪転機のジャッカルども

terms.gloss: Subbotniks: voluntary unpaid work days (originally Saturdays) of the early Soviet period.
terms.why_hard: Not 'Saturdays' or 'overtime'; needs a short in-line gloss the first time.

proposed.ja: スボートニク（無償奉仕労働日）

terms.gloss: The open-air produce market ('Privoz' in Odessa usage) that Treukhov wants to clear from the city; the word is an Odessa regionalism.
terms.why_hard: Not 'import market'; a farmers' market where goods are brought in by cart.

proposed.ja: 青物市場

terms.gloss: Tossing a hero in the air by the crowd in celebration; Treukhov, Gavrilin, Mosin and Polesov are all 'качали'.
terms.why_hard: English has no single verb; use one fixed phrase across the book (Polesov is tossed twice that day).

proposed.ja: 胴上げされる

terms.gloss: About six poods, i.e. roughly 100 kg; why Gavrilin does not fly high.
terms.why_hard: Convert once, consistently, without a footnote; keep the unit only if the book-wide rule keeps Russian units.

proposed.ja: ゆうに百キロ

terms.gloss: The outlying district of Stargorod where the tram depot stands, beyond the railway bridge.
terms.why_hard: Fictional toponym; transliterate consistently and decline it as a place in the target language.

proposed.ja: グシーシチェ

terms.gloss: The ninth anniversary of the October Revolution, 7 November 1926; the tram opening slips to May Day 1927.
terms.why_hard: 'October' alone is opaque; render as the anniversary of the Revolution, and keep 'May Day' for Первое мая.

proposed.en: the ninth anniversary of the October Revolution
proposed.ja: 十月革命九周年

conventions: Soviet acronyms and portmanteau bodies (губисполком, НКПС, Пищетрест, Старкомхоз): render as a descriptive institutional name on first mention with the transliterated form in parentheses only when the body recurs; never leave raw Latin-alphabet acronyms in zh or ja.

Dialogue: Russian em-dash paragraphs become quotation marks in en (double), 中文引号 “ ” in zh and 「 」 in ja, one paragraph per speaker as in the original; quoted newspaper prose stays in guillemet-style quotes rendered as « » in en and as 《》/『』 titles only for publications.

Address: 'товарищ' is always 'Comrade' / 同志 / 同志 (after the surname in zh and ja); Gavrilin's ты to Treukhov is shown by informal register (ja plain form, no さん), while narrator asides keep the mock-solemn formal register in all three languages.

meta.summary: object with keys [rank, terms, chapter_titles, conventions, page_types]

terms.gloss: The protagonist, a former marshal of the nobility, now a registry-office clerk; the narrator alternates between surname and name-and-patronymic
terms.why_hard: The alternation Воробьянинов / Ипполит Матвеевич is a deliberate mock-formal rhythm; collapsing both to one form, or adding Mr./さん, flattens the tone

proposed.en: Ippolit Matveyevich Vorobyaninov (alternate 'Vorobyaninov' / 'Ippolit Matveyevich' exactly as the Russian does)
proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫（沃罗比亚尼诺夫／伊波利特·马特维耶维奇）
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビャニノフ（ヴォロビャニノフ／イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ）

terms.gloss: Vorobyaninov's mother-in-law, dying in chapter 2; 'мадам Петухова' in the chapter title, 'теща' and 'старуха' in narration
terms.why_hard: Three labels for one woman (name, теща, старуха) must stay distinct but recognisably the same person; 'мадам' is a pre-revolutionary honorific used with irony

proposed.en: Klavdia Ivanovna Petukhova; 'Madame Petukhova'; 'his mother-in-law'; 'the old woman'
proposed.zh: 克拉夫季娅·伊万诺夫娜·彼图霍娃；彼图霍娃夫人；岳母；老太太
proposed.ja: クラウディヤ・イワーノヴナ・ペトゥホワ；ペトゥホワ夫人；姑（しゅうとめ）；老婆

terms.gloss: The town's drunken coffin-maker, 'гробовых дел мастер', who follows Vorobyaninov hoping for an order
terms.why_hard: His trade title 'гробовых дел мастер' is a mock-guild formula; also a real Volga town name, but here just a comic surname to transliterate

proposed.ja: ベゼンチュク、棺桶職人

terms.gloss: The rival funeral parlour, named 'Nymph'; its three owners are called 'три «нимфа»' (masculine!) as a joke
terms.why_hard: Must keep the shop name in quotes, keep 'nymph' as a word, and reproduce the joke of three bearded men being called 'nymphs'; consistent with the chapter title Безенчук и «нимфы»

proposed.ja: 葬儀店「ニンフ」；三人の「ニンフ」

terms.gloss: Bezenchuk's recurring nonsense oath, roughly 'to hell with it', a euphemistic sub-standard curse
terms.why_hard: It is a signature catchphrase repeated throughout the book; must be one fixed, slightly absurd, non-obscene formula, not a fresh curse each time

proposed.ja: 「ブランコにでも突っ込んじまえ」

terms.gloss: Father Fyodor, priest of the church of Florus and Laurus, a future rival treasure-hunter
terms.why_hard: Orthodox priestly title 'отец' should be 'Father', not 'Reverend'; the church name has Orthodox saints not familiar to the reader

proposed.ja: フョードル神父

terms.gloss: The parish church of Sts Florus and Laurus (folk form Frol and Lavr), patrons of horses
terms.why_hard: Фрол is the Russian folk form of Florus; translators either invent 'St Frol' or over-Latinise; pick one and keep it

proposed.en: the Church of St Frol and St Lavr
proposed.ja: フロルとラヴル教会

terms.gloss: The neighbour, 'the agronomist's wife' (suffix -ша = wife of), also called мадам Кузнецова; her husband is 'бородатый агроном'
terms.why_hard: -ша does not mean she is an agronomist herself; also her 'мадам' is old-regime provincial politeness

proposed.zh: 农艺师太太库兹涅佐娃
proposed.ja: 農学技師の奥さんクズネツォワ

terms.gloss: Fictional provincial town ('Old Town') where Vorobyaninov's mansion and the chairs were; central to the plot
terms.why_hard: Invented name; must be transliterated, never translated as 'Old Town', and kept identical everywhere

proposed.ja: スタルゴロド

terms.gloss: Streets of the unnamed district town of chapter 1-2 (the N-town); the square has the Zhukovsky bust
terms.why_hard: Transliterate, but keep the same scheme for all street names in the book (площадь = Square, улица = Street)

proposed.zh: 斯塔罗潘广场／奥瑟普纳亚街
proposed.ja: スタロパンスカヤ広場／オスィプナヤ通り

terms.term: бюстик поэта Жуковского («Поэзия есть бог в святых мечтах земли»)
terms.gloss: Tiny bust of the poet Zhukovsky with his line 'Poetry is God in the holy dreams of the earth', regularly chalked with an obscenity
terms.why_hard: The quotation is a real Zhukovsky line (from Camoens); the diminutive 'бюстик' is a joke; the chalked word is never printed

proposed.en: the little bust of the poet Zhukovsky; 'Poetry is God in the holy dreams of the earth'
proposed.zh: 诗人茹科夫斯基的小半身像；“诗是大地神圣梦想中的上帝”
proposed.ja: 詩人ジュコフスキーの小さな胸像；「詩とは地上の聖なる夢に宿る神なり」

terms.gloss: The barber, referred to by his shop's Frenchified sign 'Pierre and Constantine' although his name is Andrei Ivanovich
terms.why_hard: The narrator uses the shop name as a personal name in quotes; the joke is lost if translated as 'the barber'

proposed.zh: “皮埃尔与康斯坦丁”（理发师安德烈·伊万诺维奇）
proposed.ja: 「ピエールとコンスタンチン」（床屋のアンドレイ・イワーノヴィチ）

terms.gloss: Popular illustrated Moscow weekly magazine, the barber's source of 'medical' knowledge
terms.why_hard: A real magazine still published; should not be translated as 'Little Flame'

proposed.ja: 雑誌『オゴニョーク』

terms.term: бывший пролетарий умственного труда, а ныне палаточник Прусис
terms.gloss: Prusis, a former 'proletarian of intellectual labour' (Soviet term for office workers) turned NEP-era stall-keeper
terms.why_hard: 'Палаточник' is a small private trader with a market stall (a NEPman), not a tent-dweller; the official phrase is deadpan parody

proposed.en: Prusis, formerly a proletarian of intellectual labour, now a market-stall trader
proposed.zh: 普鲁西斯，从前的脑力劳动无产者，如今的摊贩
proposed.ja: プルーシス、元「頭脳労働プロレタリア」、今は露店商

terms.gloss: The social-insurance fund clinic providing free doctors to insured workers, widely distrusted
terms.why_hard: Acronym; 'insurance office' misses that it is the state clinic where the doctors come from

proposed.ja: 保険金庫の医者

terms.gloss: Workplace mutual-aid fund from which employees could take an advance or loan
terms.why_hard: Not a bank and not a charity; a small office institution the reader should recognise as 'the office loan fund'

proposed.ja: 職場の互助会

terms.gloss: Vorobyaninov's present job: clerk of the ZAGS, the Soviet civil registry office (births, marriages, deaths)
terms.why_hard: ZAGS is an acronym; a bare transliteration means nothing, while 'registrar' sounds too grand for the deliberate humiliation

proposed.ja: 戸籍登記所の書記

terms.gloss: Tsarist police versus Soviet militia (the renamed police); 'начальник милиции' recurs
terms.why_hard: Both are police forces; the joke is that the regime changed and the graffiti did not; keep two distinct words consistently

proposed.en: the police, and later the militia
proposed.ja: 警察、のちにはミリツィヤ（民警）

terms.gloss: Bezenchuk still addresses him as 'господин' (pre-revolutionary 'sir/Mr'), while narration and crowd use 'граждане'
terms.why_hard: The old-regime honorific versus Soviet 'citizen' is a recurring class marker; keep both distinct in every language

proposed.zh: “沃罗比亚尼诺夫老爷”（与“公民们”相对）
proposed.ja: 「ヴォロビャニノフの旦那」（対して「市民諸君」）

terms.gloss: Furniture by Gambs, a Petersburg maker famed for walnut suites; the twelve chairs are a Gambs drawing-room set
terms.why_hard: 'Гамбсовская' is a maker's name, not an adjective; must be fixed since the set is the book's MacGuffin

proposed.zh: 冈布斯家具的客厅成套家具
proposed.ja: ガンブス製の客間家具一式

terms.term: кисти и глазет; первый сорт, прима
terms.gloss: Coffin trimmings: tassels and glazet (brocade), sold in grades 'first class' and 'prima'
terms.why_hard: Trade jargon of the undertaker; 'глазет' is a silver-thread brocade for coffins, not glaze

proposed.en: tassels and brocade; first class or prima
proposed.zh: 流苏和银线锦缎；头等还是特等
proposed.ja: 房飾りと錦襴；一等か特等か

terms.gloss: Easter cakes, baked at home before Orthodox Easter; dates the action to Lent, spring 1927
terms.why_hard: Not generic 'cake'; the flour shortage joke depends on Easter baking

proposed.ja: 復活祭のクリーチ（菓子パン）

terms.gloss: Peaked cloth cap worn by tradesmen; the coffin-makers doff and clutch them
terms.why_hard: Not a hat and not a military cap; keep one word since it recurs as a sign of the petty bourgeois

proposed.ja: 鳥打帽

terms.gloss: Pre-war (c. 1910) fashions: the Chantecler hat and the Argentine tango, and the tango 'Amapa' of the same era
terms.why_hard: They date the mother-in-law's bonnet to a specific vanished world; leave the names, do not explain

proposed.en: the 'Chantecler' hat; the Argentine tango; the 'Tango Amapa'
proposed.zh: “尚特克莱尔”帽；阿根廷探戈；《阿玛帕探戈》
proposed.ja: 「シャントクレール」帽；アルゼンチン・タンゴ；「タンゴ・アマパ」

terms.gloss: Soviet term for a domestic servant ('household worker'), whom employment law could turn into a plaintiff
terms.why_hard: 'Maid' hides the Soviet euphemism and the joke that she could sue him

proposed.ja: 家事労働者（お手伝い）

terms.gloss: 'Regalia', Vorobyaninov's sneering word for the diamonds, with a stuttered rolled r for rage
terms.why_hard: Keep the mock-grand word and the stammer as a typographic device

proposed.ja: あんたのれ、レガリアを

conventions: Dialogue: Russian em-dash lines become double quotation marks in English, “ ” in Chinese, 「 」 in Japanese; the narrator's dry interjections mid-speech stay unmarked and in the same register.

Address: keep name-and-patronymic forms transliterated in all three languages (no さん/先生, no Mr/先生 added); render вы as polite forms and ты as familiar (Japanese plain style) so shifts like the crowd's 'Это ты, Андрей' register.

Soviet institutions and acronyms (загс, страхкасса, милиция) are rendered by a fixed descriptive English/Chinese/Japanese phrase, not transliterated, and never footnoted unless the joke depends on the original.

terms.gloss: Stargorod locksmith-mechanic, hyperactive busybody and monarchist conspirator; called by name-and-patronymic throughout
terms.why_hard: The narrator alternates his full name with mock-epithets; the target text must keep the same person recognisable under every variant and not domesticate the patronymic

proposed.zh: 维克多·米哈伊洛维奇·波列索夫
proposed.ja: ヴィクトル・ミハイロヴィチ・ポレソフ

terms.gloss: Mock-solemn epithet for Polesov, varied as слесарь-энтузиаст, гениальный слесарь, слесарь-механик
terms.why_hard: Each variant is a running joke on the same base word слесарь; the base noun must be fixed once (locksmith/mechanic) so the variations register as variations

proposed.zh: 知识分子钳工（基础词：钳工）
proposed.ja: インテリ錠前屋（基本語：錠前屋）

terms.gloss: The fortune-teller (гадалка), Vorobyaninov's former flame, keeper of the parrot
terms.why_hard: Addressed only by name-and-patronymic; her role-noun гадалка is also used as her tag by the narrator and must stay one word

proposed.zh: 叶莲娜·斯坦尼斯拉沃夫娜／女占卜师
proposed.ja: エレーナ・スタニスラヴォヴナ／占い師

terms.gloss: 1920s housing cooperative of a building's tenants, the legal party that contracts and pays for repairs
terms.why_hard: Not a 'housing association' in the Western sense nor a landlord; abbreviation should be unpacked into one stable phrase, not transliterated

proposed.ja: 住宅組合

terms.gloss: Stargorod municipal-economy department (коммунхоз), successor to the housing department, holder of the furniture archive
terms.why_hard: Also appears as коммунхоз; the two must be visibly the same office, and the town-name prefix Стар- should be kept legible

proposed.zh: 斯塔尔戈罗德市政公用局（旧市公用局）
proposed.ja: スタルゴロド市公共事業局（スタルコムホーズ）

terms.gloss: Housing department that requisitioned and redistributed bourgeois property after 1917; disbanded 1921
terms.why_hard: The plot hinges on its archive; a vague 'housing office' loses that it once occupied the girls' school and issued the furniture orders

proposed.ja: 住宅課

terms.gloss: Official allocation warrants by which requisitioned furniture was assigned to new owners
terms.why_hard: Not 'orders' or 'warrants' for arrest; this is the book's MacGuffin document and must be one fixed term

proposed.ja: 配給証

terms.gloss: Building yard-keeper who locked the gates at night and took tips (гривенники) from late-returning tenants
terms.why_hard: 'Janitor' loses the gate-keeping and the ten-kopek economy that drives the whole gate episode

proposed.ja: 庭番

terms.gloss: Ten-kopek coin, the standard late-night tip to the yard-keeper
terms.why_hard: Should stay a concrete coin, not 'a tip', and be consistent with how other kopek sums are rendered

proposed.ja: 十コペイカ銀貨

terms.gloss: Repair of Primus kerosene stoves, the universal 1920s cooking appliance; on Polesov's signboard
terms.why_hard: The signboard text recurs as physical evidence; render Primus as a brand-name noun once and reuse it verbatim

proposed.ja: プリムス修理

terms.gloss: Invented Soviet firm name, 'Quick-Pack', whose lads help drag the yard-keeper away
terms.why_hard: A joke acronym that must sound like a real NEP enterprise; transliteration alone kills the gag

proposed.ja: 「即包」

terms.gloss: Soviet militia officer (the regular police, renamed after 1917); район/отделение are the local station
terms.why_hard: 'Militiaman' suggests paramilitary to a modern reader; 'policeman' loses the era but is understood

proposed.ja: 民警（警察分署）

terms.gloss: Polesov's bureaucratese 'in the presence of the absence of', now a Russian proverb
terms.why_hard: Must be a grammatically absurd but plausible officialese phrase, not smoothed into 'since there are no'

proposed.en: Given the presence of an absence of
proposed.ja: …の不在が存在する以上

terms.gloss: Insult meaning boor, upstart lout; ex-gentry usage sneering at the lower classes
terms.why_hard: Polesov shouts it at the yard-keeper as a class insult; 'ham' is a false friend, 'boor' keeps the class edge

proposed.ja: 下司野郎！

terms.gloss: Folk curse: 'seven-fathered viper', a viper of unknown paternity
terms.why_hard: The narrator reuses it deadpan as an epithet for Polesov, so the curse must be a repeatable noun phrase

proposed.ja: 七人父の毒蛇

terms.gloss: Former marshal of the nobility (предводитель), now shaven of his moustache; the 'sam Vorobyaninov' of the conspirators
terms.why_hard: Предводитель is 'marshal of the nobility', a pre-revolutionary elected post; rendering it as 'leader' or 'ringleader' breaks Korobeinikov's question

proposed.en: Ippolit Matveyevich Vorobyaninov; the (former) marshal of the nobility
proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫；前贵族首席代表
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーヴィチ・ヴォロビヤニノフ；元貴族団長

terms.gloss: Narrator's recurring epithet for Ostap Bender, the schemer
terms.why_hard: The most famous tag in the book; must be one fixed phrase everywhere, not paraphrased per context

proposed.ja: 偉大なる策士

terms.gloss: Bender's mock-commercial name for the pair (also компаньоны, концессия), parodying NEP concession contracts
terms.why_hard: The joke is that a treasure hunt is framed as a state concession; keep 'concession' as the base word in every variant

proposed.ja: 利権屋たち／コンセッション

terms.gloss: Member of the Soviet Union of Trade Employees, per the union card of Konrad Karlovich Mikhelson
terms.why_hard: Acronym must read as a real union, and the contrast with 'Senator Mikhelson' must survive

proposed.en: member of the Soviet Trade Employees' Union
proposed.zh: 苏维埃商业职员工会会员
proposed.ja: ソヴィエト商業従業員組合員

terms.gloss: 'Non-Party', the standard official label for a citizen not in the Communist Party
terms.why_hard: Not 'independent' or 'apolitical'; it is a fixed line on Soviet documents

proposed.ja: 非党員

terms.gloss: To register one's residence with the militia, required at hotels
terms.why_hard: Explains why Vorobyaninov needs a fake identity; 'check in' misses the police registration

proposed.ja: 居住登録をする

terms.gloss: Stargorod furnished-rooms hotel with a grandiose name; neighbouring rooms are «Ливадия», the tsar's Crimean palace
terms.why_hard: The pretentious names are the joke; keep 'Sorbonne' and 'Livadia' as names, not translated

proposed.ja: 貸間「ソルボンヌ」

terms.gloss: Fictional provincial town ('Old Town') where the first part is set; suburb Гусище
terms.why_hard: Transliterate, never translate; keep prefix consistent with Старкомхоз

proposed.zh: 斯塔尔戈罗德（古西谢区）
proposed.ja: スタルゴロド（グシーシチェ）

terms.gloss: Chancellery of the pre-revolutionary city governor (градоначальник), Korobeinikov's old employer
terms.why_hard: Must read as a tsarist office distinct from the Soviet ones so Bender's jab lands

proposed.ja: 旧市長官官房

terms.gloss: 'Citizen', the Soviet official address replacing господин
terms.why_hard: Bender uses it with formal irony; keep 'Citizen' capitalised as a title in all three languages

proposed.ja: 市民コロベイニコフ

terms.gloss: Literally 'ladybird'; figuratively a meek simpleton
terms.why_hard: Bender's 'don't be a ladybird' must keep the insect image or the pun on cows is lost

proposed.ja: テントウムシみたいにおとなしくするな

terms.gloss: French-inflected 'Maman', gentry usage Bender adopts to pose as an aristocrat's son
terms.why_hard: Should keep the French colouring, not become plain 'mother'

proposed.ja: ママン

conventions: Dialogue: Russian em-dash lines become double quotes in en, “” in zh, 「」 in ja; no honorifics (-san etc.) added in ja, patronymics kept in all three languages
Bender's archaic polite particle -с (Почему-с) is rendered by a mock-deferential tag ('Why not, sir?', 「なぜです、旦那」, “为什么不，老爷？”) rather than dropped
The stray line 'Категория:Двенадцать стульев (Ильф и Петров)' on page 38 is a wiki artefact, not text, and is omitted from all translations

terms.gloss: The young con man, co-protagonist; the narrator's 'великий комбинатор'
terms.why_hard: Spelling must be fixed once across all three scripts; zh/ja transliterations vary between editions

proposed.ja: オスタップ・ベンデル

terms.gloss: Narrator's recurring epithet for Bender: the great schemer/operator
terms.why_hard: Proverbial in Russian; must be one fixed phrase, not paraphrased differently each time; 'combinator' is a false friend

proposed.ja: 大策士

terms.gloss: Former marshal of the nobility, Bender's partner; addressed by name-and-patronymic throughout
terms.why_hard: Patronymic must be kept (it carries class and formality); Bender's 'дорогой патрон' and 'предводитель' are separate epithets

proposed.zh: 伊波利特·马特维耶维奇·沃罗比亚尼诺夫
proposed.ja: イッポリート・マトヴェーエヴィチ・ヴォロビヤニノフ

terms.gloss: Narrator's running name for Bender and Vorobyaninov, from Bender's calling the chair hunt a 'концессия' (NEP foreign-capital concession)
terms.why_hard: Not 'partners': the NEP-era legal term is the joke; needs one fixed rendering with a single note at first occurrence

proposed.ja: 利権屋たち

terms.gloss: Chapter XIII title; the newsreel director's stock command to his subjects, now a Russian catchphrase
terms.why_hard: Must match wherever it recurs in the chapter; the second-person plural directorial imperative is the humour

proposed.ja: 深く息を吸って——あなたは興奮している！

terms.gloss: Chapter XIV title; Bender's fake monarchist underground, parodying Isaiah's 'swords into ploughshares' (перекуём мечи на орала)
terms.why_hard: 'Орало' is a Church Slavonic ploughshare, not 'shouting'; the biblical echo must survive in each language

proposed.en: The Union of the Sword and the Ploughshare
proposed.ja: 剣と鋤の同盟

terms.term: гигант мысли, отец русской демократии и особа, приближенная к императору
terms.gloss: Bender's mock-grand billing of Vorobyaninov to the conspirators; proverbial in Russian
terms.why_hard: Recurs verbatim and in fragments through the book; must be fixed word for word so the reader recognises the refrain

proposed.en: a giant of thought, the father of Russian democracy, and a person close to the Emperor
proposed.zh: 思想巨人、俄国民主之父、皇帝身边的近臣
proposed.ja: 思想の巨人、ロシア民主主義の父にして皇帝の側近

terms.gloss: Supporter of Grand Duke Kirill Vladimirovich, who proclaimed himself Emperor in exile in 1924
terms.why_hard: Reads as a random surname without context; needs a compact gloss so Polesov's 'Так точно' lands as a monarchist oath

proposed.en: a Kirillite (a supporter of Grand Duke Kirill, the émigré pretender)
proposed.zh: 基里尔派（拥护流亡大公基里尔称帝者）
proposed.ja: キリル派（亡命皇帝を称するキリル大公の支持者）

terms.gloss: NEP tax-form category: a self-employed artisan operating a powered machine; used as Polesov's epithet
terms.why_hard: It is a bureaucratic classification, not a description; the joke is the form-language applied to a man

proposed.en: a sole-trader artisan with motor (a NEP tax category)
proposed.zh: 有动力设备的个体手工业者
proposed.ja: 動力付き個人手工業者

terms.gloss: Narrator's epithet for Polesov, the fussy mechanic who owns a workshop and never finishes a job
terms.why_hard: 'Слесарь' is a fitter/mechanic, not only a locksmith; 'интеллигент' is a social type, not 'intelligent'

proposed.ja: インテリ鍵屋

terms.gloss: Stargorod mechanic, monarchist busybody, guide to the fortune-teller's flat
terms.why_hard: Referred to alternately by surname, name-patronymic and epithets; all must resolve to one person

proposed.zh: 维克托·米哈伊洛维奇·波列索夫
proposed.ja: ヴィクトル・ミハイロヴィチ・ポレソフ

terms.gloss: Fortune-teller (гадалка), Vorobyaninov's mistress of 1899, hostess of the conspirators
terms.why_hard: Her name is Polish; keep patronymic, and render 'гадалка' consistently (fortune-teller, not 'witch')

proposed.zh: 叶莲娜·斯坦尼斯拉沃夫娜（女占卜师）
proposed.ja: エレーナ・スタニスラヴォヴナ（占い師）

terms.gloss: Коммунальное хозяйство: the town's municipal-services department, where Treukhov works
terms.why_hard: A Soviet acronym the reader must understand at sight; do not transliterate bare

proposed.ja: 市公共事業局（コムホーズ）

terms.gloss: Soviet office employee; used in 'сопричисленного к лику совработников', parodying 'причислен к лику святых' (canonised)
terms.why_hard: The pun on canonisation must be carried; a flat 'Soviet employee' loses it

proposed.en: Soviet office worker (miraculously canonised among the ranks of)
proposed.zh: 苏维埃机关工作人员（奇迹般被列入其“圣列”）
proposed.ja: ソヴィエト機関職員（奇跡的にその「列聖」を受けた）

terms.gloss: Elected member of the pre-revolutionary city duma (municipal council)
terms.why_hard: 'Гласный' is not 'vocal/public'; the reader must see a tsarist-era rank now politically compromising

proposed.en: councillor of the old City Duma
proposed.ja: 旧市会（市ドゥーマ）議員

terms.gloss: Dyadyev's NEP-era private firm; a mock Soviet portmanteau ('Quick-Pack')
terms.why_hard: Transliteration alone hides the joke; keep the name and gloss its meaning once

proposed.ja: ブィストロウパク（「速包」商会）

terms.gloss: Kislyarsky's cooperative: an Odessa ring-bread guild trading under a Moscow name; the geography is the joke
terms.why_hard: Бублик and баранка are both ring breads; the contradiction Odessa/Moscow must stay visible

proposed.zh: 敖德萨面包圈合作社“莫斯科小圈饼”
proposed.ja: オデッサ・ブブリキ組合「モスクワ・バランキ」

terms.gloss: 'Jupiter' arc floodlights used by 1920s film crews
terms.why_hard: Not the planet or a name; must be a film lighting term in each language

proposed.ja: ジュピター・ライト（撮影用アーク灯）

terms.gloss: Bender's mock-fashionable label for anything pretentiously up to date
terms.why_hard: Attributed to Bender as his catchword; render identically every time

proposed.ja: 「シック・モダン」

terms.term: акробаты фарса, гиены пера, виртуозы ротационных машин
terms.gloss: Treukhov's drunken philippic against the bourgeois press; the phrases became proverbial
terms.why_hard: Parody of Soviet newspaper invective; keep the triple structure and mock-grandeur

proposed.en: these acrobats of farce, these hyenas of the pen, these virtuosos of the rotary press
proposed.zh: 这些闹剧的杂技演员，这些笔杆子的鬣狗，这些轮转印刷机的大师
proposed.ja: 茶番の軽業師ども、ペンのハイエナども、輪転機の名手ども

terms.gloss: Polesov's mangled bureaucratese ('given the presence of absence'); a proverbial phrase
terms.why_hard: Must sound like a stalled official formula, not be smoothed into sense

proposed.en: In view of the presence of absence…
proposed.ja: 不在の存在に鑑みまして……

terms.gloss: Formula of tsarist decrees ('has been graciously pleased to command'), the only imperial phrase Bender can recall
terms.why_hard: Needs a recognisably archaic court register in each target

proposed.en: has been graciously pleased to command
proposed.ja: 恩恵をもって命じ給うた

terms.gloss: Komsomol, the Communist youth league; the director's shouted pose for the girl on camera
terms.why_hard: Komsomol should be a fixed proper noun across the book, not paraphrased

proposed.ja: コムソモールからのご挨拶！

terms.gloss: Horse-drawn cab and its driver, still the ordinary urban transport in 1927
terms.why_hard: Not a taxi; the trams-versus-cabs contrast is the chapter's point

proposed.ja: 辻馬車

terms.gloss: Stargorod lane where Polesov and the fortune-teller live (house No. 5)
terms.why_hard: One transliteration for the street throughout; 'переулок' rendered as lane consistently

proposed.ja: ペレレシンスキー横丁

conventions: Dialogue: keep the Russian dash in the source line; en uses double quotes, zh uses “ ”, ja uses 「 」; narrator's mock-solemn asides stay in the same register with no added exclamation.

Names: keep name + patronymic wherever the Russian has it; en transliteration BGN-style (Vorobyaninov, Matveyevich), zh via standard Xinhua tables with ·, ja katakana with ・; do not add -san in ja to Russian name-patronymic forms.

Address: 'господин' (Polesov, pre-revolutionary) → en 'Mister', zh '先生', ja '様'; 'товарищ' → en 'Comrade', zh '同志', ja '同志'; ты/вы shifts are shown in ja by plain vs です・ます style, in en/zh by tone only.
